title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical errors. The claims (D = S mod diagonal translation is a 2-element set, sections of S over D are in bijection with A, the incidence embeddings) check out on the explicit model. The page is a draft with crossed-out false starts, and the duality is asserted rather than verified.

ideas.what: Equivalence between F_2^C-torsors and degree-2 covers A -> C, with S = sections of A over C, and the dual construction D = S/diagonal with A = sections of S over D
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of the square: vertex/edge duality, the outer automorphism of the dihedral group D_4, and torsors under F_2^C

ideas.what: Three 2-element sets (codiagonals C, diagonals D, orientations omega) whose contracted product is trivial
ideas.modern_name: The three nontrivial characters of D_4^ab ≅ (Z/2)^2 summing to zero; F_2-torsor (contracted-product) calculus
ideas.where_published: Torsor/contracted-product formalism is standard in SGA / Giraud; this specific formulary appears unpublished

ideas.what: Incidence embeddings S ↪ P_2(A) and A ↪ P_2(S)
ideas.modern_name: Incidence structure (bipartite 8-cycle) of the vertices and edges of a 4-gon

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, functorial (torsor-theoretic) presentation of elementary combinatorics: the square, D_4 as 2-Sylow of S_4, and its abelianization. It is presumably preparation for level-2 / Γ_0(4)-type structures on elliptic curves. It is characteristic of Grothendieck's style, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Under C, D, omega the labels read 'codiagonales', 'diagonales', 'orientations' (not 'codimensionnels', 'degrés').
'A ↪ F_2(S)' should be 'A ↪ 𝔓_2(S)' (set of 2-element subsets of S), mirroring S ↪ 𝔓_2(A) on the previous page.
'(≃ sections de S sur D)' is correct; the strike-through next to (S_d)_{d∈D} seems to begin '𝔓 ... S' rather than 'F_2 ... sur S'.
'(D ≃ S/≃_S)' and '(C ≃ A/≃_A)' denote quotients by the canonical fixed-point-free involutions (written S/a_S, A/a_A on the next page).
The opening '1' at the top is a section/sub-item marker, not a formula.
